report.source_text: He was started on pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) with 2 tablets of lipase-protease-amylase (24 000–76 000–120 000 units) by mouth 3 times a day with meals. His diarrhea improved 2 months after initiation of PERT, allowing him to regain weight to his previous baseline while reducing his caloric intake to 1800 to 2000 calories per day.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man with a 35-year history of Roux-en-Y bypass and type 2 diabetes presented with 8 months of new-onset severe diarrhea (10–15 oily, greasy stools per day with foul-smelling gas), resulting in 41-kg weight loss despite consuming five 1000-calorie meals per day. He also reported progressive muscle weakness and recurrent falls. Physical examination revealed weight 84 kg (BMI 26.8), mild bilateral triceps and iliopsoas weakness, and bilateral peripheral edema to the knees. Diagnostic workup demonstrated fecal elastase <40 μg/g and a 48-hour fecal fat study showing massive steatorrhea (277 g in 24 hours). CT enterography revealed marked pancreatic atrophy without evidence of pancreatic malignancy. The patient was diagnosed with exocrine pancreatic insufficiency and initiated on pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) with 2 tablets of lipase-protease-amylase (24,000–76,000–120,000 units) three times daily with meals. His diarrhea improved 2 months after PERT initiation, allowing weight regain to baseline while reducing caloric intake to 1800–2000 calories per day.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Severe steatorrhea with fecal elastase diagnostic of EPI
Marked pancreatic atrophy on imaging consistent with pancreatic insufficiency
Clinical presentation of malabsorption with progressive weight loss and muscle weakness
Dramatic clinical response to PERT with symptom resolution and weight recovery
